content: {"id": "b5da5620-43bc-463a-8411-beed1d778eed", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "I'm reviewing the security posture of our Amazon Bedrock setup with a read-only misconfiguration assessment. For the least-privilege IAM check, iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies succeeds and shows no role attaching AmazonBedrockFullAccess, but iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies returns AccessDenied. What status does it report?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "9f6b7fb1-c365-4a8f-b24e-7b25c7c86128", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The check shouldn't report a pass. Based on what you've described, the honest status is **inconclusive** (also called "unable to verify" or "partial"). It should not be "compliant" or "no findings".

- **Roles:** `ListAttachedRolePolicies` succeeded and showed no role with `AmazonBedrockFullAccess`. That clears roles only.
- **Users:** `ListAttachedUserPolicies` returned AccessDenied. The assessment can't see whether any user has the policy attached, so that part is unverified. Missing permissions don't mean there's no finding.
- **Overall result:** A pass on the roles plus an unverified result on users can't add up to a clean pass. The check should say something like "No violations found in roles. Users could not be evaluated (AccessDenied on iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies)."

I don't know the exact status label your tool or framework uses. I only have the behavior you described, and I can't see its status vocabulary. If it only offers pass and fail, an access error should usually map to its error, not-applicable, or unknown state, not to pass.

The check also has gaps beyond this one error:

- **Groups:** `iam:ListAttachedGroupPolicies` would show users who inherit the policy through a group.
- **Inline and customer-managed policies:** A policy that grants `bedrock:*` doesn't show up as an `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` attachment. A least-privilege check should look for broad Bedrock actions like `bedrock:*` as well.
- **Permissions to add:** To close the gap, grant the assessment role read-only access to `iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies`, `iam:ListAttachedGroupPolicies`, and `iam:ListEntitiesForPolicy`. `ListEntitiesForPolicy` on the `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` ARN shows every user, group, and role attached to it in one call.

If you tell me which tool runs this check, I can help work out how it handles access errors. I can also run the read-only `ListEntitiesForPolicy` call in an account this agent space can access.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
